subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What side-effect boundary should OpenClaw guarantee for cron and skills dry-run/testing, and should that boundary share a request-scoped contract with global agent dry-run?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementation would define a user-trusted no-side-effects boundary plus new public CLI, Gateway, protocol, and possible config semantics across cron, skills, tools, hooks, channels, and external APIs.

options.title: Design one request-scoped core contract
options.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool-interception semantics together so preview modes make the same side-effect guarantees across runtime paths.

options.title: Ship a narrow cron validator first
options.body: Add only cron config, schedule, and delivery validation while leaving skill testing and global tool interception to separate decisions.

options.title: Defer broad dry-run semantics
options.body: Keep current command-specific dry-run surfaces until a maintainer sponsors the broader trusted preview boundary.

recommendation.title: Design one request-scoped core contract
recommendation.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool-interception semantics together so preview modes make the same side-effect guarantees across runtime paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combined signal from prior issue review plus history across skills CLI, cron, and shared tool execution surfaces.
